title: Assess civic developments by purpose and meaningful audience change
summary: Compose source-backed civic stage assessments with explicit research, monitored-action or opportunity objectives, then deliver only an actionable or meaningfully changed assessment to the correct audience. Audience preferences never alter underlying facts or authority.
in_scope: Quiet, digest, correction and concrete decision-request reasons
out_of_scope: A universal civic importance or legal-confidence score
Treating every incomplete assessment as a question for the user
implementation: Define purpose inputs for monitored subjects, territory/service match, responsible owner, deadlines and known dispositions, with versioned field meanings and source provenance.
Compose stage/evidence/authority conclusions first; evaluate objective consequences separately and record the inputs responsible for each difference.
Compare with the last applicable assessment delivered to the same audience, including corrections and changed authority/source coverage; reused assessments retain their original evidence identity.
Apply named attention treatments and withholding reasons; missing information becomes a bounded evidence request or unresolved status unless a concrete human decision is required.
Revalidate source/profile/assessment freshness immediately before existing delivery handoff and preserve delivery/consumption/action distinctions.

Use the synthetic monitoring scenario pack as illustrative planning input for company, special-interest and school-district contexts. Preserve provision-specific source positions separately from host-approved client positions; unknown is not neutral. Expected decisions remain outside model-visible packets. Host-owned optional LLM investigation and custom wording follow the admitted assessment without changing facts or bypassing freshness/delivery gates.

acceptance.criterion: Two audiences can receive different attention from identical civic evidence without divergent source facts.
acceptance.verification: Run researcher and service-fit audience fixtures and compare their shared factual assessment digest and separate consequence/delivery receipts.

acceptance.criterion: Only a changed actionable predicate, correction or declared boundary creates a repeat update.
acceptance.verification: Replay repeated agenda references, new solicitation deadline and later cancellation; verify the notification sequence and quiet reasons.

acceptance.criterion: Missing authority or source coverage does not become an approval claim or automatic user request.
acceptance.verification: Use unavailable evidence and unreviewed authority controls; inspect unresolved and permitted-next-read output.

acceptance.criterion: A correction queued against obsolete evidence is withheld or regenerated before emission.
acceptance.verification: Change the relevant source/profile between selection and delivery and check the dependency/freshness receipt.

tests: Same project inside versus outside audience territory
New purchasing deadline already handled by assigned owner
Cancellation after an earlier delivered opportunity
Unchanged event repeated through another source
Same source evidence across company, advocacy and school-district IT/finance work contexts; a host context change alone changes only the affected audience consequence.
Provision-specific proponent/opponent/neutral/unknown positions; no actor stance inferred from a keyword, organization name or collective result.
Optional host writer failure, newly gathered evidence, stale source/context and revoked access preserve existing factual monitoring and refuse unsupported custom alerts.
risks: Service-fit preferences can contaminate source interpretation if evaluated in the same unstructured prompt.
Too-aggressive quietness can hide a corrected prior claim.

reuse.application: Retain matter versus purpose/audience assessment as the domain-independent design boundary.
Use the hypothetical access-control project progression only as an invented conformance scenario.
Twelve invented chronological checkpoints and four audience/work contexts with explicit expected decisions; not an executed test or qualified corpus.

Reuse existing isolated historical replay, domain cutoff, paced Next controls and inspectable delivery sink. The current two statewide scenarios report model_mode unavailable; Matter/local scenario support remains integration work.

Reuse host-owned assessment enrichment, exact-evidence readers and supported synthesis when adding a later short custom-alert writer; no replacement client, alert stream or production deployment is implied.

Authored structured inputs are separate from the expected trace and contain no provider responses. StateCivics KS-1105 executed the installed Matter attention primitive through existing replay and in-app capture at f412e3415; this is bounded host mechanism evidence, not completion of civic adaptation or provider qualification.
